abstract.text:
The vacuum expectation values of conserved currents play an essential role in the generalized
hydrodynamics of integrable quantum field theories. We use analytic continuation to extend these
results for the excited state expectation values in a finite volume. Our formulas are valid for
diagonally scattering theories and incorporate all finite size corrections.

abstract.text:
The vacuum expectation values of conserved currents play an essential role in the generalized
hydrodynamics of integrable quantum field theories. We use analytic continuation to extend these
results for the excited state expectation values in a finite volume. Our formulas are valid for
diagonally scattering theories and incorporate all finite size corrections.

supercut.text: The paper starts from generalized hydrodynamics and its TBA description, where vacuum expectation values of conserved charges and currents are encoded through an occupation-number pairing.

The collection of the β i “temperatures” can be traded for the expectation values of the conserved charges hq i i ∝ ∂ β i log Z, implying that the expectation values of the currents hj i i depend on hq i i which is the equation of state hj i i = F i (hqi).
The key formal object is the pairing with occupation-number measure, which implements the TBA convolution and dressing.

To go to excited states, the authors use analytic continuation of the TBA equations.
It was observed in [14] that excited state TBA equations can be obtained from the ground-state one by analytical continuations.
Thus we expect that all formulae remain the same as the groundstate ones except that the pairing has to be replaced with a new pairing:
Formally we can represent the effect of the continuation with a modified contour as shown on Figure 1.

Replacing the pairing in the vacuum formulas gives the excited-state charge and current expectation values; the authors then reduce them to expressions separating physical particles from quasi-particles.
These are the main results of the paper.
Since they were not really derived, merely conjectured based on previous experiences, we perform various consistency checks and elaborate the details.
The main current formula is then rewritten with polynomial and exponential finite-size corrections separated, and checked against earlier asymptotic results and the excited-state LM formula.
This formula is the main result of our paper, which describes the exact finite volume expectation value of conserved currents.
This formula agrees with the recent direct calculations in [8, 9].
We also checked these formulas in the sinh-Gordon theory against the generalization of the LM formula for excited states [17].
Our results provide all the finite size corrections to the asymptotical formulas valid in a diagonally scattering integrable theory with a single species.
